title: Guangzhou's Most Decorated Hall: the Roof, or the Carvings? | China Travel Expert
description:
Guangzhou's Chen Clan Ancestral Hall might be the most heavily decorated building in China — and visitors split over what to photograph: the riot of ceramic figures running along the rooflines, or the carved screens and beams inside.

Finished in 1894, the compound is nineteen halls, courtyards and corridors in classic Lingnan style. Chen families from across Guangdong pooled money to build it as a shared ancestral temple AND a boarding academy, where clansmen could prepare for the imperial civil-service exams. Its roof ridges are packed with Foshan Shiwan ceramic figures — entire opera and folk scenes modelled in glazed clay — while the halls below show off wood, brick and stone carving on almost every surface. Today it's the Guangdong Folk Art Museum.

★ Expert Tip: go on a bright day and bring a zoom. The best detail is 8–10 m up on the roof ridges — the Shiwan figure scenes read as a blur to the naked eye but come alive through a lens.

广州陈家祠（陈氏书院）1894 年落成，广东各地陈氏合资而建，既是合族祠堂，也是族人备考科举的书院。屋脊上满是佛山石湾陶塑的戏曲人物，厅堂里木雕、砖雕、石雕铺满梁枋。今天是广东民间工艺博物馆。你会先拍屋顶，还是先拍厅堂的雕刻？
